svg.title: Our life is frittered away by detail.

text.tspan: Everyday English - B2 - 2026/10/28 - Quote - 01

svg.title: A simple workspace leaves fewer competing demands on attention.

text.tspan: A simple workspace leaves fewer competing demands on attention.
Our life is frittered away by
detail.
Henry David Thoreau (first-person narrator) · Henry David Thoreau ·
Walden, Where I Lived, and What I Lived For · Published 1854
After explaining why he went to the woods, Thoreau
turns to the many small demands of ordinary life. He
urges readers to simplify their affairs. His complaint is
about attention being scattered across countless
concerns, rather than directed towards what matters.
The sentence is deliberately forceful. It need not
mean that every detail is worthless: some details
protect people or make work reliable. The useful
question is which demands deserve our limited time.
Frittered away suggests something valuable being
lost a little at a time. Detail is treated as an
overwhelming accumulation here, rather than as one
particular small fact.
Name one unnecessary detail you could simplify and
one important detail you would keep. (Model: I could
stop adjusting a routine message's layout repeatedly,
but keep the date and meeting place clear.)
